artist.introduction: Olivier Kéros is a 23-year-old passionate artist from Berlin who deliberately positions himself outside the classical art school and mainstream. In his 14-square-meter apartment, which he has transformed into a studio, he creates works that impress with their extraordinary size, as well as their remarkable use of color and form. His art not only defies the confined conditions of his living space but also his background, which has been shaped by poverty. For Kéros, art means saying 'yes' to life and welcoming transformation, as change is the only constant. His personal philosophy is reflected in his belief that every crisis simultaneously represents a new beginning.
artist.autodidact: The self-taught artist found his way to art definitively through his psychology studies at the age of about 20, although he had already engaged with creative processes since childhood. His works are characterized by process-oriented dynamism, strong contrasts, and unique motifs that challenge viewers to engage with the unconscious
artist.purpose: Kéros's paintings not only raise new questions but also open deeper levels of awareness. In his art, he emphasizes the vitality and diversity of painting processes. He consciously forgoes traditional techniques of figurative painting or radically reinterprets and simplifies them to the edge of minimalism. Through the deliberate use of bold colors and seemingly simple forms, he conveys direct and immediate emotions.
artist.style: This leads to a style that could be described as abstract expressionism. Kéros combines technical skill with deep dedication, making his works both emotionally and intellectually appealing. They constantly challenge the viewer and leave room for individual interpretations. With his unique approach, he creates art that goes far beyond aesthetics and encourages reflection on personal perception.
